title: Semantic Encapsulation Violation (Hidden Assumptions)
pattern: Caller code relies on hidden, undocumented implementation assumptions of a class, such as skipping a setup step because they know another part of the system has already run it.
why_bad: It introduces silent, tight coupling. If the internal implementation of the class changes (e.g., the bootstrapper no longer initializes that specific database instance), the caller code breaks silently at runtime.
detection: A client program calling a method on an object without satisfying the public prerequisites specified in the interface, relying on contextual knowledge.
counterexample: None. This is a pure encapsulation bug.
fix: Make the interface robust: enforce prerequisites programmatically (e.g., using Typestate pattern or internal initialization checks on first query) so the object can never be called in an invalid state.
source: Steve McConnell, *Code Complete* (2004), Chapter 6, Section 6.2 ("Be wary of semantic violations of encapsulation").
